subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — Limitation of Liability and Termination Refunds
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: FintechCo Legal <contracts@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline — liability cap interaction with termination refunds

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the call this morning. We've attached our third-pass redline of the MSA and the Order Form (FintechCo_MSA_redline_v3.docx). Two related items popped up in our internal review and legal asked me to confirm Redwood's position before we proceed to signature:

1) Limitation of Liability vs. Termination Refunds — your MSA currently caps liability at the greater of USD 1M or 12 months of fees. Is that cap intended to limit any refunds due to early termination of prepaid fees (Order Form prepaid annual subscription), or should termination refunds be treated as a separate payment outside the cap?

2) Wind-down assistance — the Order Form includes a short wind-down assistance obligation in Section 6. If we terminate for convenience or if the service is terminated for cause, are fees for wind-down assistance considered damages under the cap or payable outside the LoL?

We are trying to avoid ambiguity that would make our procurement/legal team push back on the cap applying to refunds. Can you confirm Redwood's standard practice? If Redwood considers refunds outside the cap, please share suggested redline language so we can move quickly.

Appreciate it — happy to set a quick 30-min sync if easier.

Best,
Olivia Grant
Head of Procurement, FintechCo
Attachment: FintechCo_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline — liability cap interaction with termination refunds

Thanks Olivia — received and reviewing now. Sharing a quick, candid take so you and your counsel have something to react to before we get legal fully looped in:  

- Our commercial preference is that refunds for unused prepaid subscription fees are a contractual payment (not "damages") and therefore should be carved out from the general liability cap. That keeps customer-facing refunds predictable and unambiguous.
- Wind-down assistance is trickier. We typically offer a narrowly-scoped, time-limited transition assist (e.g., up to 10 hours of engineer time or a defined runbook) and treat fees for that work as payable amounts outside of LoL only if the termination is for our material breach. For convenience terminations, we prefer refunds for unused prepaid fees but not an open-ended obligation to provide indefinite winding services.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I'll loop in Legal with a suggested redline snippet.
2) Can you confirm whether FintechCo requires a pro-rata refund (standard) or a full refund of the remaining prepaid term? That will affect the commercial drafting.
3) If helpful, let's book a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize.

For clarity: I want to avoid creating an exception so broad that it swallows the LoL — e.g., making every monetary payment outside the cap. But customer refunds for unused prepaid fees are common carveouts and we can accommodate with explicit calculation language.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_FintechCo_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Suggested redline and rationale — LoL carveouts for refunds/wind-down

Dylan / Marissa,

Draft snippet below that I think balances commercial expectations and legal risk. Feel free to pass to FintechCo with a short note. I attached a Word doc with the redline snippet (Proposed_MSA_snippet_Redwood_v1.docx).

"Suggested clause (for insertion in Limitation of Liability section):

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitation of liability set forth in Section X shall not limit or exclude (i) amounts properly payable by Customer as a refund of prepaid Fees for unused subscription services under the Order Form (calculated pro rata based on unused days in the paid term), and (ii) amounts expressly payable under Section Y (Wind-Down Assistance), but only to the extent such amounts are: (A) expressly identified in a written invoice; and (B) incurred within the forty-five (45) day period following termination.

Rationale: 
- Carving out prepaid refunds as a separate contractual payment reduces ambiguity for procurement (they have a dollar they can expect back).
- For wind-down assistance, we limit both scope and time (45 days) to avoid open-ended operational exposure.
- Keep the general LoL cap for consequential and indirect damages; do not carve those out.

A couple of points for commercial: 
- If FintechCo insists on a full refund of the remaining term rather than pro-rata, we should consider negotiating the cap upward or adding a short notice requirement (e.g., 30-day termination notice) to manage impact.
- We should preserve exceptions for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and third-party IP indemnity — those remain outside cap per standard practice.

Happy to tweak the language.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Attachment: Proposed_MSA_snippet_Redwood_v1.docx (docx)
"

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial constraints — refund size and timing

Team,

Quick commercial input from renewals perspective: we cannot accept an open-ended obligation that refunds the entire remaining prepaid term without a meaningful limit. Customers sometimes ask for full refunds and then reopen months later — operationally painful. My suggestions:

- Keep pro-rata refund (unused days) as default.
- Cap refund calculation to the remaining prepaid fees but do not treat other damages as outside the LoL.
- If they insist on full-term refunds, tie that to either: (a) an increased liability cap for the deal (we can agree to USD 2M for strategic accounts), or (b) require a 30-day termination notice for convenience.

Also, wind-down assistance should be: 
- Defined scope (runbook + up to 15 engineer-hours), and
- Billed at standard hourly SOW rates if beyond the included hours. That way procurement gets predictability, and we avoid an unlimited obligation.

If we push the 45-day timebox too hard with FintechCo, they will ask for longer — consider a hard limit with an escalating rate after 45 days as an alternative.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline — liability cap interaction with termination refunds (proposed language)

Olivia — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal stakeholders together. Below is the consolidated position and proposed redline. We think this should resolve procurement's ambiguity while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure.

Proposed redline (to insert in Limitation of Liability):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitation of liability set forth in Section X shall not limit or exclude (i) refunds of prepaid Fees for unused subscription services under the Order Form, which shall be calculated on a pro rata basis for the unused portion of the paid term, and (ii) amounts expressly payable for Wind-Down Assistance under Section Y, provided that such Wind-Down Assistance is: (A) limited to work described in the Order Form or an agreed runbook; (B) either completed within forty-five (45) days following termination or billed in accordance with Redwood's standard rates; and (C) invoiced no later than sixty (60) days after the effective date of termination."

Commercial guardrails: 
- Refunds are pro rata only; full-term refunds are not standard unless we agree to a higher cap or special commercial terms.
- Wind-down assistance is time-boxed (45 days) and limited in scope; any extra work is billable.
- Usual exceptions (gross negligence, willful misconduct, IP indemnity) remain outside the cap as standard.

If FintechCo is comfortable with this phrasing, we'll provide a redlined MSA and Order Form reflecting the snippet and remove ambiguity around calculation and timing. Please let me know whether FintechCo requires pro-rata (recommended) or full-term refunds — if it's full-term, we need to agree an elevated liability cap or notice mechanics.

Happy to jump on a quick call to finalize.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_MSA_snippet_Redwood_v1.docx (docx)
